skill.name: wsdiscovery
skill.description: Guides authorized WS-Discovery scans to discover and enumerate ONVIF cameras, NVRs, printers, and IoT devices on a network.
skill.summary: Discover authorized WS-Discovery devices and summarize ONVIF metadata.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick alerts are Markdown command examples, but the skill clearly guides network discovery and device enumeration. Confirmed risk centers on authorization, target scope, multicast discovery, and collection of device inventory details.

remediation.suggestion: Require users to confirm authorization, ownership, and exact target scope before any scan.
Validate hostnames and IP addresses, avoid shell interpolation, and reject targets outside approved ranges.
Warn users to protect serial numbers, firmware versions, and service endpoints from public sharing.
Add a caution that multicast discovery can enumerate many devices and needs explicit approval.

content.value_statement: Network teams need a fast way to identify WS-Discovery devices during authorized checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through scoped discovery and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of the wsdiscovery command with target hosts or IP addresses.
Supports text, quiet, and JSON output modes.
Explains verbose collection of full XML responses.
Identifies device IP addresses, ports, UUIDs, types, and service endpoints.
Highlights ONVIF camera, NVR, printer, and media device discovery use.
limitations: Only finds devices that support WS-Discovery and respond on the selected network.
Requires the wsdiscovery tool from the iothackbot bin directory.
Can expose sensitive device inventory, so use only with authorization.
Does not perform exploitation, password testing, or remediation.

use_cases.title: Audit lab cameras
use_cases.description: Inventory authorized ONVIF cameras and capture models, firmware versions, and management endpoints for review.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot discovery
use_cases.description: Check whether cameras, printers, or media devices respond to WS-Discovery on a known network segment.

use_cases.title: Prepare asset records
use_cases.description: Collect device identifiers and service details for controlled IoT inventory documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Check one device
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wsdiscovery to check one authorized camera IP. Summarize discovered device details and note if no response appears.

prompt_templates.title: Compare output modes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an authorized WS-Discovery check and explain which output mode is best for a human report.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory a lab segment
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover authorized WS-Discovery devices in my lab scope. Summarize IP addresses, device types, firmware versions, and service endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Assess exposed metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm scope, use verbose output where needed, and produce a risk-focused report with service endpoints and firmware details.

output_examples.input: Authorized check for one camera at a known lab address.
output_examples.output: The report lists one ONVIF device, its UUID, model, firmware version, and management service endpoint.

output_examples.input: Network administrator asks why a camera is not found.
output_examples.output: The response explains that the device may not support WS-Discovery, multicast may be blocked, or the wrong segment was selected.

output_examples.input: Security reviewer requests verbose discovery findings.
output_examples.output: The summary separates device metadata, exposed management URLs, and follow-up checks that need written authorization.

best_practices: Confirm authorization and exact scope before running any discovery command.
Prefer the smallest target range that answers the operational question.
Store device identifiers, firmware versions, and service endpoints in restricted records.
anti_patterns: Scanning public or third-party networks without permission.
Running multicast discovery across broad networks without an approved scope.
Sharing serial numbers, firmware versions, or service endpoints in public channels.

faq.question: What does this skill help me find?
faq.answer: It helps find WS-Discovery devices such as ONVIF cameras, NVRs, printers, and media devices on authorized networks.

faq.question: Does it run the scan by itself?
faq.answer: It guides the assistant to use the local wsdiscovery command when the tool is installed and permitted.

faq.question: Can I use it on public networks?
faq.answer: Use it only on systems you own or have written permission to assess.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The source instructions describe text, quiet, and JSON output modes.

faq.question: What data can appear in results?
faq.answer: Results may include IP addresses, ports, UUIDs, models, firmware versions, serial numbers, and service endpoints.

faq.question: Does it exploit devices?
faq.answer: No. The instructions cover discovery and enumeration, not exploitation or credential testing.
